newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Buoyant Portuguese shares ready for further gains.
newsitem.headline: Buoyant Portuguese shares ready for further gains.

text.p: Portuguese stocks can extend strong first quarter gains, analysts say, providing that there are no fresh shocks over the European single currency or U.S. interest rate policy.

Since the beginning of the year, the BVL general index, which covers all stocks quoted on the Lisbon exchange, has risen 16 percent, while the PSI20 measure of leading blue chips has gained 17 percent, helped by the country's positive economic outlook.
"Portugal has to decouple from the States, not least because its economic fundamentals are pretty positive," said analyst James Harrison of Lisbon brokers Midas Corretora.

Steadily easing inflation, prospects for further Portuguese interest rate falls and the generally good performance of companies all justified investment in stocks and the continued switching out of bonds by investment funds, analysts say.
Harrison said the BVL Geral .BVLG could rise a further 26 percent before the end of the year, underpinned by an average growth in earnings per share (EPS) of 27 percent.
Espirito Santo Research analyst Jose Freire saw room for share price gains of five to 10 percent by June.

"I don't think that the market is expensive. It is pretty accurately valued. In coming months, the market is going to be influenced by (the European Union's proposed) monetary union and the evolution of U.S. interest rates," added another analyst who asked not to be named.
"If investors...look at the (company) results for 1996 and the first numbers for 1997, there is potential for gains," said Freire.
But the analysts added that the recent market turbulence could take its toll on the banks which still account for some 25 percent of the Lisbon bourse index.
"January and February were good trading months for the banks but March was less positive," Freire said.
Nuno Thomaz of brokers Titulo Corretora saw EPS growth of 30 percent in 1997.
He noted that the coming privatisation of a part of EDP-Electricidade de Portugal in what will be the largest such operation to date in Portugal would also give a sharp push to bourse capitalisation.
"The passage from emerging market to small European market will draw important funds to the market," he said.
"If Portugal is included in the MSCI 14-Europe (Morgan Stanley Capital International index) these other investors are going to start looking at Portugal," he added.

Analysts say that Portugal meets economic tests for membership of the key Morgan Stanley stock index but that in the past, market liquidity had probably not been considered sufficient for its inclusion.
